findings.body: The failed unified-storage call is observed in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds instead of dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, so storage error rate/latency dashboards under-report storage failures and legacy metrics show phantom errors for a call that never touched legacy.
findings.failure_mode: Observability data is attributed to the wrong backend, misleading operators during incidents.
findings.impact: The failed unified-storage call is observed in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds instead of dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, so storage error rate/latency dashboards under-report storage failures and legacy metrics show phantom errors for a call that never touched legacy.
findings.root_cause: Copy of the mode1 error-path metric call without switching the recorder to the storage histogram when the operation order was inverted for mode 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Change this call to d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to match the timer (startStorage) and the store that failed.
findings.title: Create error path records storage failure in the legacy duration metric
findings.trigger: Any Create request where d.Storage.Create returns an error in mode 3.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 45 shows `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` when `d.Storage.Create` fails. The timer is `startStorage` and the failed call is to Storage, but the metric recorded is LegacyDuration. Comparing to mode1 line 46 which correctly uses `recordLegacyDuration` for legacy failures, this is clearly wrong - storage failures should use `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.body: A unified-storage update failure is recorded in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds with is_error=true, while dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds never records the failure, corrupting per-store error metrics.
findings.failure_mode: Per-store latency/error histograms are mislabeled, hiding storage-side regressions.
findings.impact: A unified-storage update failure is recorded in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds with is_error=true, while dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds never records the failure, corrupting per-store error metrics.
findings.root_cause: Wrong metric recorder used on the storage error branch, inconsistent with the success branch immediately below which uses recordStorageDuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).
findings.title: Update error path records storage failure in the legacy duration metric
findings.trigger: Any Update request where d.Storage.Update returns an error in mode 3.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 129 shows `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` when `d.Storage.Update` fails. findings.body: Legacy delete-collection latency and errors are observed in dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, double-counting storage timings and leaving legacy async failures invisible in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds.
findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
findings.failure_mode: Async legacy write failures cannot be detected from metrics, defeating the stated safety-net purpose of mode 3.
findings.impact: Legacy delete-collection latency and errors are observed in dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, double-counting storage timings and leaving legacy async failures invisible in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds.
findings.root_cause: The asynchronous legacy branch reuses the storage recorder while timing the legacy call (startLegacy).
findings.suggested_fix: Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) inside the goroutine.
findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records into the storage duration metric
findings.trigger: Any successful DeleteCollection in mode 3, where the spawned goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 166 shows `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` inside the goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`. The timer is `startLegacy` but the recorder is `recordStorageDuration`. Should be `recordLegacyDuration` to match the operation being timed.

findings.body: dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds gains one time series per deleted object name, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality growth, and the `kind` label no longer holds a kind so queries grouping by kind break for delete.
findings.failure_mode: Metric cardinality explosion and unusable per-kind delete latency queries.
findings.impact: dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds gains one time series per deleted object name, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality growth, and the `kind` label no longer holds a kind so queries grouping by kind break for delete.
findings.root_cause: The name variable was passed into the metrics helper parameter that populates the `kind` label.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name, matching the error branch on the preceding lines and all other mode 3 call sites.
findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name as the `kind` label value
findings.trigger: Every successful Delete in mode 3; `name` is the per-object resource name (e.g. a playlist UID) while the histogram label is declared as "kind".
findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 shows `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` where `name` is passed as the third argument. Per metrics.go:59, the third parameter is the `kind` label. Line 103 correctly uses `options.Kind` for the error case. Passing object name as kind causes unbounded cardinality.

pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Mode 3 will work the following way:

reads (get, list) : only use unified storage
writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) : write to unified storage and then asynchronously, write to legacy, just as a safe measure.

**Why do we need this feature?**

[Add a description of the problem the feature is trying to solve.]

**Who is this feature for?**

[Add information on what kind of user the feature is for.]

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/search-and-storage-team/issues/53

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.

raw_findings.body: The asynchronous legacy write is aborted with context canceled, so legacy storage silently misses created/updated/deleted rows, breaking the mode 3 guarantee that legacy is kept in sync as a safety measure.
raw_findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legacy store drifts out of sync with unified storage without any error surfaced to the caller.
raw_findings.impact: The asynchronous legacy write is aborted with context canceled, so legacy storage silently misses created/updated/deleted rows, breaking the mode 3 guarantee that legacy is kept in sync as a safety measure.
raw_findings.root_cause: Background goroutines are parented to the cancellable request-scoped context instead of a detached context.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or context.Background() plus the needed request values) before applying WithTimeoutCause, in all four mode 3 goroutines (create, update, delete, delete-collection).
raw_findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request completes
raw_findings.trigger: A normal Create request in mode 3: the handler returns as soon as storage succeeds, the apiserver cancels the request context, and the still-running goroutine's derived context is cancelled before or during d.Legacy.Create.

raw_findings.body: Concurrent read/write on the same object triggers a data race (detectable under -race) and can corrupt the response body or the value written to legacy.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Nondeterministic data race between the request handler and the async legacy writer.
raw_findings.impact: Concurrent read/write on the same object triggers a data race (detectable under -race) and can corrupt the response body or the value written to legacy.
raw_findings.root_cause: The shared request object escapes to a goroutine that outlives the synchronous call without copying.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Deep-copy the object before the goroutine (objCopy := obj.DeepCopyObject()) and pass the copy into the closure, as DualWriterMode1.Create already does with createdCopy.
raw_findings.title: Create passes the caller-owned object to the background legacy write without a deep copy
raw_findings.trigger: The apiserver handler continues to read or mutate the request object (e.g. serialization of the response, admission/finalizer post-processing) while the spawned goroutine concurrently hands the same *runtime.Object to legacy storage, which mutates metadata during its own create path.

raw_findings.body: Downstream log lines lose the name/kind/method key-values that were just built into `log`, making delete failures hard to correlate; every other method in this file stores `log`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reduced diagnosability of delete operations due to missing structured log fields.
raw_findings.impact: Downstream log lines lose the name/kind/method key-values that were just built into `log`, making delete failures hard to correlate; every other method in this file stores `log`.
raw_findings.root_cause: The enriched logger variable was built but the unenriched receiver logger was placed in the context.
raw_findings.title: Delete puts the bare d.Log into the context instead of the enriched logger
raw_findings.trigger: Any Delete call in mode 3 where downstream code retrieves the logger via klog.FromContext(ctx).

raw_findings.body: Legacy can end up with a different object than unified storage (or fail resource-version precondition checks), silently diverging the two stores; the removed code explicitly wrapped objInfo with the storage result via updateWrapper.
raw_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
raw_findings.failure_mode: Data divergence between unified and legacy storage on update.
raw_findings.impact: Legacy can end up with a different object than unified storage (or fail resource-version precondition checks), silently diverging the two stores; the removed code explicitly wrapped objInfo with the storage result via updateWrapper.
raw_findings.root_cause: The updateWrapper indirection that propagated the storage-written object to legacy was dropped when the write order was inverted.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the storage result before the async legacy call, e.g. pass &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res} (using a deep copy of res) to d.Legacy.Update.
raw_findings.title: Legacy Update receives the raw upstream objInfo instead of the object already written to storage
raw_findings.trigger: An Update request in mode 3 where objInfo is a patch/apply-style UpdatedObjectInfo: legacy re-evaluates objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own stale object rather than the object just persisted in unified storage.

raw_findings.body: The defining behavior of mode 3 — writing to legacy asynchronously — is untested; a regression that drops or cancels the legacy write (as the request-scoped goroutine context can) would keep all tests green.

finding.title: Playlist "mode 3" integration subtests do not actually run in mode 3
finding.trigger: Starting Grafana with DualWriterDesiredModes = Mode3: SetDualWritingMode defaults currentMode to Mode1 and only implements the Mode1<->Mode2 transitions (see the "#TODO add support for other combinations" comment), so Mode3 is never selected.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that mode 3 is never selected relies on SetDualWritingMode logic, but the patch adds integration tests that pass DualWriterDesiredModes with Mode3. validated_findings.body: The failed unified-storage call is observed in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds instead of dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, so storage error rate/latency dashboards under-report storage failures and legacy metrics show phantom errors for a call that never touched legacy.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Observability data is attributed to the wrong backend, misleading operators during incidents.
validated_findings.impact: The failed unified-storage call is observed in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds instead of dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, so storage error rate/latency dashboards under-report storage failures and legacy metrics show phantom errors for a call that never touched legacy.
validated_findings.root_cause: Copy of the mode1 error-path metric call without switching the recorder to the storage histogram when the operation order was inverted for mode 3.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change this call to d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to match the timer (startStorage) and the store that failed.
validated_findings.title: Create error path records storage failure in the legacy duration metric
validated_findings.trigger: Any Create request where d.Storage.Create returns an error in mode 3.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 45 shows `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` when `d.Storage.Create` fails. The timer is `startStorage` and the failed call is to Storage, but the metric recorded is LegacyDuration. Comparing to mode1 line 46 which correctly uses `recordLegacyDuration` for legacy failures, this is clearly wrong - storage failures should use `recordStorageDuration`.

validated_findings.body: A unified-storage update failure is recorded in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds with is_error=true, while dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds never records the failure, corrupting per-store error metrics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Per-store latency/error histograms are mislabeled, hiding storage-side regressions.
validated_findings.impact: A unified-storage update failure is recorded in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds with is_error=true, while dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds never records the failure, corrupting per-store error metrics.
validated_findings.root_cause: Wrong metric recorder used on the storage error branch, inconsistent with the success branch immediately below which uses recordStorageDuration.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).
validated_findings.title: Update error path records storage failure in the legacy duration metric
validated_findings.trigger: Any Update request where d.Storage.Update returns an error in mode 3.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 129 shows `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` when `d.Storage.Update` fails. Same pattern as candidate 0 - storage failure recorded to legacy metric. Line 132 correctly uses `recordStorageDuration` for success, confirming the error path is inconsistent.

validated_findings.body: Legacy delete-collection latency and errors are observed in dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, double-counting storage timings and leaving legacy async failures invisible in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds.
validated_findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Async legacy write failures cannot be detected from metrics, defeating the stated safety-net purpose of mode 3.
validated_findings.impact: Legacy delete-collection latency and errors are observed in dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds, double-counting storage timings and leaving legacy async failures invisible in dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds.
validated_findings.root_cause: The asynchronous legacy branch reuses the storage recorder while timing the legacy call (startLegacy).
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) inside the goroutine.
validated_findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records into the storage duration metric
validated_findings.trigger: Any successful DeleteCollection in mode 3, where the spawned goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 166 shows `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` inside the goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`. The timer is `startLegacy` but the recorder is `recordStorageDuration`. Should be `recordLegacyDuration` to match the operation being timed.

validated_findings.body: dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds gains one time series per deleted object name, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality growth, and the `kind` label no longer holds a kind so queries grouping by kind break for delete.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Metric cardinality explosion and unusable per-kind delete latency queries.
validated_findings.impact: dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds gains one time series per deleted object name, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality growth, and the `kind` label no longer holds a kind so queries grouping by kind break for delete.
validated_findings.root_cause: The name variable was passed into the metrics helper parameter that populates the `kind` label.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name, matching the error branch on the preceding lines and all other mode 3 call sites.
validated_findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name as the `kind` label value
validated_findings.trigger: Every successful Delete in mode 3; `name` is the per-object resource name (e.g. a playlist UID) while the histogram label is declared as "kind".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 shows `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` where `name` is passed as the third argument. Per metrics.go:59, the third parameter is the `kind` label. Line 103 correctly uses `options.Kind` for the error case. Passing object name as kind causes unbounded cardinality.

validated_findings.body: The asynchronous legacy write is aborted with context canceled, so legacy storage silently misses created/updated/deleted rows, breaking the mode 3 guarantee that legacy is kept in sync as a safety measure.
validated_findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
validated_findings.failure_mode: Legacy store drifts out of sync with unified storage without any error surfaced to the caller.
validated_findings.impact: The asynchronous legacy write is aborted with context canceled, so legacy storage silently misses created/updated/deleted rows, breaking the mode 3 guarantee that legacy is kept in sync as a safety measure.
validated_findings.root_cause: Background goroutines are parented to the cancellable request-scoped context instead of a detached context.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or context.Background() plus the needed request values) before applying WithTimeoutCause, in all four mode 3 goroutines (create, update, delete, delete-collection).
validated_findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request completes
validated_findings.trigger: A normal Create request in mode 3: the handler returns as soon as storage succeeds, the apiserver cancels the request context, and the still-running goroutine's derived context is cancelled before or during d.Legacy.Create.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 51 shows `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` deriving from the request context. When the parent request completes and its context is cancelled, the derived context will also be cancelled, potentially aborting the legacy write. Mode1 has the same pattern but there it's acceptable since storage is secondary; in mode3 legacy sync is the stated purpose.

validated_findings.body: Concurrent read/write on the same object triggers a data race (detectable under -race) and can corrupt the response body or the value written to legacy.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Nondeterministic data race between the request handler and the async legacy writer.
validated_findings.impact: Concurrent read/write on the same object triggers a data race (detectable under -race) and can corrupt the response body or the value written to legacy.
validated_findings.root_cause: The shared request object escapes to a goroutine that outlives the synchronous call without copying.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Deep-copy the object before the goroutine (objCopy := obj.DeepCopyObject()) and pass the copy into the closure, as DualWriterMode1.Create already does with createdCopy.
validated_findings.title: Create passes the caller-owned object to the background legacy write without a deep copy
validated_findings.trigger: The apiserver handler continues to read or mutate the request object (e.g. serialization of the response, admission/finalizer post-processing) while the spawned goroutine concurrently hands the same *runtime.Object to legacy storage, which mutates metadata during its own create path.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim requires that the apiserver handler mutates the object after Create returns while the goroutine is running. However, the patch shows `return created, err` returns the storage-created object, not `obj`. The goroutine uses `obj` (the input). Without evidence that `obj` is mutated post-return or that `d.Legacy.Create` mutates it in a racing way, this is speculative.

validated_findings.body: Downstream log lines lose the name/kind/method key-values that were just built into `log`, making delete failures hard to correlate; every other method in this file stores `log`.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Reduced diagnosability of delete operations due to missing structured log fields.
validated_findings.impact: Downstream log lines lose the name/kind/method key-values that were just built into `log`, making delete failures hard to correlate; every other method in this file stores `log`.
validated_findings.root_cause: The enriched logger variable was built but the unenriched receiver logger was placed in the context.
validated_findings.title: Delete puts the bare d.Log into the context instead of the enriched logger
validated_findings.trigger: Any Delete call in mode 3 where downstream code retrieves the logger via klog.FromContext(ctx).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 97 shows `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` while line 96 builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(...)`. The enriched logger `log` is not stored in context; `d.Log` (unenriched) is. All other methods in the file use `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. This is a clear copy-paste error.

validated_findings.body: Legacy can end up with a different object than unified storage (or fail resource-version precondition checks), silently diverging the two stores; the removed code explicitly wrapped objInfo with the storage result via updateWrapper.
validated_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Data divergence between unified and legacy storage on update.
validated_findings.impact: Legacy can end up with a different object than unified storage (or fail resource-version precondition checks), silently diverging the two stores; the removed code explicitly wrapped objInfo with the storage result via updateWrapper.
validated_findings.root_cause: The updateWrapper indirection that propagated the storage-written object to legacy was dropped when the write order was inverted.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the storage result before the async legacy call, e.g. pass &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res} (using a deep copy of res) to d.Legacy.Update.
validated_findings.title: Legacy Update receives the raw upstream objInfo instead of the object already written to storage
validated_findings.trigger: An Update request in mode 3 where objInfo is a patch/apply-style UpdatedObjectInfo: legacy re-evaluates objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own stale object rather than the object just persisted in unified storage.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 139 shows `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` passing the raw `objInfo` to legacy. The old code (visible in patch context L101-L103) used `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` to pass the already-written object. Mode2 at line 298 still uses updateWrapper. Without the wrapper, legacy re-evaluates objInfo against potentially stale data.

validated_findings.body: Inconsistent test setup: this subtest registers the same collectors into a throwaway registry, and it is the only reason the prometheus import is needed in this file, making the file diverge from the established pattern and confusing future edits.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/consistency defect in newly added tests.
validated_findings.impact: Inconsistent test setup: this subtest registers the same collectors into a throwaway registry, and it is the only reason the prometheus import is needed in this file, making the file diverge from the established pattern and confusing future edits.
validated_findings.root_cause: A local registry was left in one subtest while the rest of the suite standardized on the shared registry.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete this line and use the package-level `p` variable, dropping the now-unused prometheus import.
validated_findings.title: TestMode3_Get shadows the package-level prometheus registry
validated_findings.trigger: Running TestMode3_Get; every other mode 3 subtest (and the mode1 test after this patch removed its local registry) uses the shared package-level `p`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a stylistic/consistency observation about test setup. The local registry doesn't cause functional issues - it's valid to create a new registry per subtest. The claim of 'diverging from established pattern' is subjective and doesn't constitute a bug with concrete impact.

validated_findings.body: The defining behavior of mode 3 — writing to legacy asynchronously — is untested; a regression that drops or cancels the legacy write (as the request-scoped goroutine context can) would keep all tests green.
validated_findings.evidence: m.On("Create", mock.Anything, input, mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(exampleObj, nil)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent regression of the async legacy path passes CI.
validated_findings.impact: The defining behavior of mode 3 — writing to legacy asynchronously — is untested; a regression that drops or cancels the legacy write (as the request-scoped goroutine context can) would keep all tests green.
validated_findings.root_cause: Tests were written against the synchronous return value only, with no barrier for the goroutine that performs the legacy write.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Synchronize on the legacy call (e.g. have the legacy mock signal a channel and wait for it, or use assert.Eventually with m.AssertCalled(t, "Create", ...)) before finishing each mode 3 write subtest.
validated_findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests never verify the asynchronous legacy write
validated_findings.trigger: Running TestMode3_Create (and the Delete/DeleteCollection/Update variants): the legacy expectation is registered but the test returns immediately after the synchronous storage call, before the spawned goroutine runs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap observation, not a bug in the patch. The tests may be incomplete but that's a quality concern, not a defect introduced by the patch. The patch adds new functionality; incomplete test coverage doesn't make the implementation wrong.
